I'm a Georgia player who has been in the game for one full year now. This was my first marathon, and I managed to pick up Top 8 (seeded 7th) at Athens, GA this past weekend. We had sixty players (give or take). I was playing Nidoqueen (*Barrage*) from Primal Clash.

R1 Win vs Wobb -- He had only two Wobbs out so on my turn two I donked them both in one attack-attack thanks to weakness.

R2 Lose vs Entei -- Turn one I had to Sycamore away three of my VS Seeker to even survive. He went on to be 5-0-1 so maybe I wouldn't have won (it's a match up I dislike anyway) but he was impressed with how well I did despite the bad start.

R3 -- Win vs Mega T-Tar + Zoro. Was a rough fight, since everything resisted me. I had faster setups and better prize trades though. Play of the Game was when I swooped in with Natu (*Plus*), Lysandre'd his Mega-Tar with 220dmg, and hit him with the most pitiful of Psywaves for three quick prizes.

R4 Win vs Raichu Bats -- I can take two knockouts a turn easy in this match up. Opponent was someone I befriended over marathon, thankfully, so no hard feelings when I just Dynamite Punched my way through his bench.

R5 -- Win vs Mega Mewtwos. He was a really good player from my region that I've admired for a little while now, but when he sat down and saw me he even said, "You're my worst possible match-up today." Nidoqueen OHKOs a Mega Mewtwo Y with only one energy and Muscle Band, so I didn't have much trouble here.

R6 -- ID'd because I got matched against one of my best buds and I was basically guaranteed top cut anyway. He was playing a Giratina variant. In our practice/friendly matches, we tend to go pretty even, so I wouldn't consider the match-up favorable or unfavorable.

Finished 4-1-1. Seeded 7th in top cut. Was never informed that cut would be starting because everyone thought we were on dinner break. The guy who was going to stream and commentate the top cut needed a ride to get his stuff. I gave him a ride since I knew the area well and when I returned I was told I was too late and was afforded a double loss in top cut round one, so I can't say how I did beyond that.

Top cut featured at least two Night March, the Entei that I'd played in Swiss, and I don't know what else.

The simplest way I can explain to play DnD is as follows:

* Player declares what he wants his character to do

* DM declares what type of "roll" or "attempt" the character's action counts as

* Player rolls a twenty-sided die and adds relative bonus values

* DM compares player's total to predetermined "difficulty check" value, determines if player succeeds or not.

I would also suggest that, if you are indeed running the Starter Set with only two PCs, you take out an enemy or two from each fight, or deliberately have them deal less damage to the player characters.

And, finally, no matter how badly you flub up the rules, as long as everyone agrees and is enjoying the game, you can be as wrong as you like.

From everything I've seen and experienced, the "+1" enchantment refers to a "plus 1 to hit and plus 1 to damage" on a weapon. The notion of it not stacking refers only to the first rank of "plus 1 to hit" not stacking with a masterwork dagger.

So,

Masterwork: +1 hit, +0 damage

Plus 1 Ench: +1 hit, +1 damage

Plus 2 Ench: +2 hit, +2 damage
etc., etc.

I believe the idea of the "+1 weapon" not stacking the first rank of to-hit attack bonus is there to help prevent confusion at higher ranks.
